author: Daniel Levy

Another October 7 anniversary is being observed in jarringly discordant ways
across the small strip of land formerly British Mandatory Palestine, and far
further afield. At home in London on that weekend three years ago, seemingly
irreconcilable emotional attachments demanded sustenance. The weekend passed
speaking to friends in Israel as they awaited news of those potentially
missing. Many spent the following days attending funerals of colleagues, pals,
and loved ones killed during the assault; many then campaigned for the release
of those Israelis held in Gaza.

As that Saturday bled into Sunday, the chilling rhetoric of Israel's
leadership was impossible to ignore - threatening to collectively punish the
entire civilian population of Gaza. Knowing the source of those threats, and
the history of the state's actions, the sense of foreboding was gripping.
Palestinian colleagues were also on the end of the phone that weekend: 'What
should we say?' Even as the enormity of what was unfolding became clear, there
was still hope the worst could be prevented. But there was to be no such
respite.

Within less than 100 days, I would sit sobbing quietly, listening to the
testimonies of the remarkable legal team assembled by the government of South
Africa presenting their case at the International Court of Justice in The
Hague to prevent and punish crimes of genocide being committed by Israel in
Gaza. As [Blinne Ni Ghralaigh](https://youtu.be/dqmcqCjkxaA?si=-UL-
IG00kTtfDi27), [Adila
Hassim](https://youtu.be/wACdjHO29_E?si=E510YLLFsX_WGwyG), [Tembeka
Ngcukaitobi](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=grGHum5vU74) and [Max du
Plessis](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=umwX-yF74cg), among others, detailed
the ongoing actions being undertaken by a state claiming to carry the
imprimatur of Jewish continuity, born out of the Holocaust, the impact was at
times overwhelming.

Now, on this third anniversary of October 7, Israel is preparing for its first
election since those events, to be held in three weeks' time. New revelations
are swirling about warnings Israel's leadership may have received at the time
regarding an impending attack. The timing of these new exposes - a call from
the [UAE leader](https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/israel-
security/2026-09-08/ty-article-magazine/.highlight/netanyahu-got-an-explicit-
warning-before-oct-7-he-didnt-brief-security-
chiefs/000001a0-7a3b-d7d5-a9fc-7eff3d0f0000), a hurried visit from the
[Egyptian intelligence chief](https://www.theatlantic.com/national-
security/2026/09/egypt-israel-gaza-hamas-palestinian-october-7/688720/) - is
more than a little suspect in the context of the fevered election campaign. It
seems that even for Israel's most ardent regional collaborators, the penchant
of the current coalition for bloodthirsty rhetoric and action has become
inconvenient.

The problem with all of this reportage is that it continues to ask the wrong
question.
